name: Infectious Diseases
boundaries: Infectious Diseases: fundamental discoveries and enabling technologies within this field. Include cross-field consequences where the central advance belongs to this field; exclude routine incremental optimization. Use the historical breakthroughs in the prompt to calibrate revolutionary impact.

original_dispositions.reason: The clinically meaningful broad-spectrum capability is retained; a single target effective against every RNA and DNA virus is unproven and is not assumed.

original_dispositions.original_title: Viral latency circuitry and reservoir eradication
original_dispositions.reason: Covered in part. HIV and HBV cures are distinct concrete outcomes. A common switch or complete circuitry for all persistent viruses is not established, and the entries do not claim to cure herpesviruses.

Reliable, intervention-changing forecasts would be consequential, but the proposed “any genome” prediction of spillover, evolution and transmissibility remains too unconstrained to specify a convincing general capability on the evidence reviewed. As a limitation of present models, Kato et al., “Hidden challenges in evaluating spillover risk of zoonotic viruses using machine learning models,” Communications Medicine, 2025, DOI 10.1038/s43856-025-00903-w, discussion: the dataset could not distinguish human infectivity from human-to-human transmissibility, and models missed important lineages. Full text: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12092720/.
Covered in part. These address practical responses to resistance without asserting indefinite resistance immunity or effectiveness against all bacteria.

original_dispositions.original_title: Single-dose cure of active and latent TB
original_dispositions.reason: One-dose treatment remains a particularly ambitious target; active and latent infection require separate evidence.
The entry preserves the transformative prevention concept without requiring lifelong sterile immunity as the only qualifying outcome.

Covered in part. It retains malaria-vector modification or suppression. It does not assert reversibility, absence of ecological harm, permanent elimination, or an achieved solution for Aedes-borne diseases.
Added in narrowed form. Prevention of a major, well-defined share is testable and potentially transformative; a single mechanism covering every syndrome is unestablished.
Added as INF-15, with overlap with INF-06. Neither perfect specificity nor absence of resistance is assumed.

original_dispositions.original_title: New class of infectious agents or transmission mechanisms
original_dispositions.reason: Discovery could transform the field, but the historical entry does not identify a specific disease-causing principle or intervention to demonstrate. As evidence that unusual biological entities can be found without establishing human disease causation, Zheludev et al., “Viroid-like colonists of human microbiomes,” Cell, 14 November 2024, DOI 10.1016/j.cell.2024.09.033, pp. 6521–6522: describes previously uncharacterized RNA elements in microbiomes, including one associated with an oral bacterium. Full paper: https://digital.csic.es/bitstream/10261/394596/1/1-s2.0-S0092867424010912-main.pdf. This is not evidence that those elements cause human disease.

reconciliation_change_log.reason: These address different interventions from the existing TB-vaccine and malaria-vector entries.
